context: Decide between the two shapes the ClickHouse item already validated, and prefer the cheaper one unless remote Velox is a real MCP use case. (a) Drop `deployment` from MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_ALLOWLIST['velox'] entirely: local is the only deployment MCP can fully describe, since `endpoint`, `gluten_jar_path` and the rest are not admissible anyway, so a caller asking for `remote` is asking for a run that cannot be configured through this boundary. (b) If remote Velox must stay reachable, mirror BENCHBOX_MCP_CLICKHOUSE_PROFILES: add a server-owned velox endpoint profile registry, accept only a profile name, resolve it in _prepare_adapter_platform_options at execution time so durable replays re-resolve, and reject `deployment='remote'` without a profile. Do NOT simply suppress the endpoint from the error text -- the connection attempt itself is the boundary crossing, not just its error message. Whichever is chosen, update tests/unit/mcp/test_schemas.py:272 and the 'Server-owned ClickHouse connection profiles' section of docs/operations/mcp-remote-security.md so the documented rule covers every connection-class option, not just ClickHouse.
description:
The ClickHouse remediation (#1510) established that a connection-class platform option must name a server-owned destination, never describe one. `velox.deployment` is classified `security_class="connection"` in MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_CONTRACT but was never brought under that rule, so an authenticated MCP caller can still steer the server at a listener the operator never approved.

Reproduced on develop 4836e3988d:
  validate_platform_options('velox', {'deployment': 'remote'}) -> {'deployment': 'remote'}   (accepted)
  _prepare_adapter_platform_options -> {'deployment': 'remote'}                              (unchanged)
  VeloxAdapter.from_config(...).endpoint -> 'sc://localhost:50051'

benchbox/platforms/velox.py:153 defaults the Spark-Connect endpoint to sc://localhost:50051 when the caller supplies none, and MCP does not allow `endpoint`, so `remote` always resolves to that fixed host-local target. benchbox/platforms/velox.py:370 then calls SparkSession.builder.remote(endpoint), and :389-393 probes reachability and raises an error whose text contains the endpoint. A caller who cannot set a port still learns whether a Spark-Connect server is listening on localhost:50051, and can cause a connection attempt to it.

This is narrower than the ClickHouse finding (one fixed port, not caller-chosen), and on a remote deployment the operator's `allowed_platforms` policy must already include velox for it to be reachable at all -- hence high rather than critical. But it is the same defect class the batch was convened to close, left open in the platform whose item (#1520) touched this exact option: #1520 closed only the enumeration half (deployment='docker' now fails closed) and left `remote` admissible.

Note that tests/unit/mcp/test_schemas.py:272 asserts `validate_platform_options('velox', {'deployment': 'remote'}) == {'deployment': 'remote'}`, so the current test suite pins the behaviour rather than questioning it. That assertion has to change with the fix.

Identified 2026-08-04 during the adversarial review of the mcp-v2-platform-options batch.

preserves.behavior: CLI and direct-constructor use of VeloxAdapter(deployment='remote', endpoint=...) keeps working unchanged; this is an MCP admission boundary, not an adapter capability change
deployment='docker' keeps failing closed with the existing explanatory hint
